frequency_question: How often does structural friction (inter-ministerial consensus delays, budgetary reallocation bottlenecks, and stakeholder pushback) prevent or delay the final notification of a major transport/industrial scheme beyond a 1-year operational window?
membership_rule: Includes all centrally sponsored or centrally initiated e-mobility, automotive manufacturing, or heavy transport incentive policies (e.g., FAME revisions, PLI automotive schemes) announced in draft or conceptual form. Excludes minor administrative circulars.

cases.name: PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry
PLI Scheme for Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 named major schemes; universe of major MHI mobility schemes in this exact category is fully enumerated for the decade.
known_gaps: Minor sub-schemes or state-level initiatives are excluded, but these do not match the federal scale.
skeleton: Total major transport/industrial subsidy frameworks proposed by the Ministry of Heavy Industries vs. those successfully gazetted within the targeted sub-three-year window.
multiplier: 5 hits out of 5 major initiatives successfully overcoming structural and inter-ministerial friction within their target windows over the past decade.
validity_reason: Bureaucratic machinery and inter-ministerial clearance protocols for heavy industrial subsidies remain stable across medium-term policy cycles.
